body:
SPIKE-83's REPORT (#2004) APPROVED BUT NOT MERGED — `aida pr ship` refused it: a live drive owns that spec and the orchestrator's independent reviewer gates the merge. The refusal is correct and I did not set the override. It will land through the drain or arrive at my gate afterwards.

THIS IS WHAT A RESEARCH SPIKE SHOULD LOOK LIKE, and I want to name why rather than just approve it.

It anticipated the objection I was forming. I was going to say that applying a ROUND fraction to tokens and to hours assumes uniform per-round cost, and that a rework round is plausibly cheaper than an initial one, making 37.4M an overestimate. Part 4 says it first — "a proportional estimate, not a claim that every round has identical usage" — and then argues the conclusion survives rather than ignoring the caveat.

It refused to produce the number everyone wants. Declining to collapse cost to one dollar figure without the model and token-class mix is the right call and the harder one; a blended figure would be quoted for months and wrong in a direction nobody could reconstruct.

I checked the arithmetic rather than trusting it: 40+19=59, 40/59=67.8%, 19×2.9M=55.1M, 19/0.75=25.3h, and 67.8% of each gives the stated tail. Internally consistent, and explicit that these are supplied inputs rather than things it measured.

MY DECISION, recorded on the spec: yes, the review round-trip is the first optimization to evaluate, ahead of model substitution. The more useful half is that we are already doing it — tonight's merges were largely review-loop reliability — so this RATIFIES the course rather than redirecting it. That is worth saying, because a spike confirming the existing plan reads too easily as having found nothing.

The conclusion is robust to its own caveat: halve the rework rounds' unit cost and the tail is still roughly half of all tokens. Model substitution would need an implausible per-token saving to beat eliminating half the rounds. I also recorded what would change my mind, so it stays falsifiable: per-round records showing rework costs under a third of an initial round would put the tail near 30% and make the levers comparable.

ONE CAUTION THE REPORT DOES NOT MAKE and I added, because the figure will be misread otherwise: 25.3 throughput-hours derives from a 0.75 merges/hour rate, which measures the whole pipeline including my gate and CI waits. It is not agent working time. Anyone computing cost-per-hour from it divides by wall-clock that includes hours nobody was working.

FILED AS DRAFT: BUG-1418. The drain exit record reports zero tokens for 57 of 92 drains, indistinguishably from a genuine zero, so it cannot serve as a cost ledger. The zeros span every outcome class, so a consumer cannot filter them out and cannot tell a cheap drain from an unmeasured one.

The spike's root cause is one condition explaining four situations that look unrelated from outside — a fully interactive drain, a foreign vendor schema, relocated logs, a truncated stream. First acceptance criterion is that zero and unknown must stop being the same value. A silent zero is worse than a missing field: summing the column yields a plausible wrong total, where a null would have forced the question. Same family as PRIN-4 and linked to it.

I also flagged #2003 held on one missing file — it adds a discipline master without the project-local copy, which collides with the parity guard in #1988, so whichever merges second goes red for the other's omission.
